EditBase

Quick manual

This manual takes you through EditBase in ten short steps, from a new document to a printed page. Everything it shows is on the screen in front of you: the toolbar along the top, the tool column down the left, the Pages and Layers bars at the right, and the menus that open when you right-click.

1 Documents and categories

Documents are kept in your EditBase folder in Files, and a category is a folder inside it, with a colour of its own. To start a document:

  1. Open the category it is to go in.
  2. Press “New document” at the top left. It starts as “Untitled document”: type its name in the box at the top of the screen, and the file takes that name.
  3. Write. It is saved by itself as you work, and “Save” or Ctrl+S saves it at once.

Drag a document on to a category to move it there, and up or down to put the documents in order. Right-click a document for “Duplicate”, “Move to…”, “Versions…” and “Share…”.

2 The paper

“Paper setup” sets the paper size, the orientation and the margins in millimetres, the body typeface and size, and the direction of the text. “Characters and lines” lays the writing on a grid, as on a manuscript sheet: say how many characters go on a line and how many lines on a page, or give the pitch in millimetres.

The header and the footer repeat on every page and can carry {page}, {pages}, {title} and {date}: the footer of this manual shows the page number that way. “Use as default for new documents” keeps the whole setup for the next document you start.

3 Writing and formatting

Choose a style for each paragraph from the list at the left of the toolbar, “Body text”, “Heading 1” and so on, and the typeface and size beside it; sizes go to a hundredth of a point. Bold, italic, underline, highlights, alignment and lists are on the second row of the toolbar; readings over words (ruby), emphasis dots, special characters and emoji are under “Marks and notes” in the tool column.

“Styles” changes how every paragraph of a kind looks, everywhere it is used: the headings of this manual are one style, with one of the twenty heading designs. “Copy the format at the cursor” takes the format of the words at the caret and puts it on whatever you select next.

4 Paragraph settings

Right-click a paragraph and choose “Paragraph settings…” for its indents, the space above and below it, the line height and a drop cap. “Start below the pictures beside it” starts the paragraph under any picture standing at its side, and “Keep with the next paragraph” keeps a heading on the same page as the words that follow it.

Tab positions, left, centred, right or decimal, are set in the Tabs tab in millimetres, or by pressing the ruler: drag a mark to move it, and drag it off the ruler to take it away. The list of keys at the end of this manual is lined up with one.

5 Pictures

Paste a picture, or drag one in from your computer. Right-click it for “Placement”:

  • “Words to its left” or “Words to its right” lets the text run round it;
  • “Keep clear above and below” gives it a line of its own;
  • “Place freely” puts it anywhere on the page, over or under the words.

“Picture properties…” sets the size and the margins in millimetres. Type the caption under the picture; it is a paragraph like any other. The Layer bar shows what stands over what.

6 Tables

Insert a table with “Insert”, at the top of the tool column on the left, then use Tab to move from cell to cell; Tab in the last cell adds a row. Right-click a cell to add or delete rows and columns, merge or split cells, and open “Cell properties…” for number format, alignment, font, borders and fill.

Tip

A table can calculate: type a formula beginning with =, as in LibreOffice Calc, for example =SUM(B2:B5). Drag across cells to choose a block of them and format it all at once.

7 Ruled lines and forms

For a form, use the ruled lines:

  1. Open “Ruled lines”, under “Drawing” in the tool column, and choose “Draw ruled lines”.
  2. Drag diagonally for a box, and press Tab while dragging to put lines inside it.
  3. Drag along a line to split a cell or to change the kind of line; “Erase ruled lines” takes lines away.
  4. Press Esc when you have finished.

Brackets, arrows and diagonal lines are drawn the same way. To spread a name across a box, choose its characters and use “Distribute evenly…”.

8 Printing and PDF

“Print / PDF” opens your browser's print dialogue with the paper already set. Turn “Headers and footers” off there, or the browser adds the date and the address of the file in the margins, and choose “Save as PDF” there to make a PDF file.

“Web preview” shows the document as a web page, and “Check the document”, in the menu at the top right, finds what is wrong with the pages before they are printed.

9 Saving, versions and settings

Earlier versions are kept; right-click a document and choose “Versions…” to see them and bring one back. A document is shared like any other file, and a whole category with “Share…” on the category; two people can then write in it at once.

“Settings”, at the bottom left, holds the choices that apply to all your documents: where they are kept, how many versions to keep, the units of the ruler, the widths of the bars, and how the Tab, Delete and Enter keys behave.

10 The AI assistant

Where the administrator has set it up with Talk-Bot, a triangle stands above the Pages and Layers bars. Press it to open the assistant, ask how to do something, or tell it what to change. What it changes is one step: Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Keys

Ctrl+S Save
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y Undo / Redo
Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U Bold, italic, underline
Ctrl+L, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+J Left, centred, right, justified
Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2, Ctrl+3, Ctrl+0 Heading 1, 2, 3; body text
Ctrl+K Hyperlink
Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H Find and replace
Ctrl+Enter Page break
Ctrl+P Print / PDF
Tab (in a table) Next cell; a new row at the end
